subject: MSA redlines: governing law, emergency relief & service-of-process (NimblePay)
messages:
From: Maya R. Cortez <maya.cortez@nimblepay.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nimblepay.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines: governing law & provisional relief (NimblePay)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking the MSA — attached are our negotiated redlines with a short summary on key items. Two points our legal team flagged that we want to resolve early:

- Governing law / forum: We propose New York law and exclusive arbitration (NY seat, AAA) for most disputes.
- Emergency/provisional relief: We want to preserve the right to seek provisional injunctive relief in court before arbitration and would like explicit consent-to-service language.

You’ll see the redline called "NimblePay_MSA_Redlines_20280621.pdf" attached. We can be flexible on the administrative forum so long as the seat and arbitration rules are NY/AAA.

Can your team confirm Redwood’s flexibility on these points? If we can agree, we’ll move to finalize the order form and signature.

Thanks,
Maya Cortez
VP, Legal — NimblePay
Attachments: NimblePay_MSA_Redlines_20280621.pdf (PDF, 72KB)

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Maya R. Cortez <maya.cortez@nimblepay.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 11:05:10 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: governing law & provisional relief (NimblePay)

Maya — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. Quick read-through and internal posture:

- Governing law: Redwood typically asks for Delaware law for US commercial customers. That said, we are open to NY law in customer-favoring cases if we can preserve certain carveouts (below).
- Arbitration vs court: We prefer arbitration for efficiency, but we must keep a carveout allowing either party to seek provisional injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction prior to any arbitration (injunctive/emergency relief carveout). Practically, this means a short clause allowing emergency relief in court without waiving arbitration.
- Service of process: consent-to-service is acceptable; we usually ask for a limited consent in the Order Form so Redwood’s corp. contact can accept service for commercial claims.

If NimblePay prefers NY arbitration seat with AAA administration, we’d consider that if the provisional relief carveout names Delaware or NY for emergency measures and the Order Form includes Redwood’s registered agent for service.

I’ve looped in Kar thik (contracts) and Laura (commercial counsel) and Irene (litigation) to confirm language. If you can share a redline with the proposed emergency relief sentence, we’ll respond with marked language.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Legal — Redwood Inference
Attachments: —

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nimblepay.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Maya R. Cortez <maya.cortez@nimblepay.com>, contracts@nimblepay.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 08:42:50 -0400
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: governing law & provisional relief (NimblePay)

Stephanie,

Thanks — quick counter-proposal from our side to keep negotiations moving:

- We will accept a carveout for provisional relief but prefer the clause to permit either party to seek emergency relief in the federal or state courts sitting in New York (in addition to arbitration for the merits).
- For service of process, NimblePay will accept a narrowly-tailored consent to service via our registered agent in NY or via email where permitted, but we want explicit assurance that Redwood won’t use service consent for unrelated collection claims.

I attached a one-page alternative that inserts a short sentence: "Notwithstanding the Agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek provisional injunctive or other provisional relief in any court of competent jurisdiction (including New York courts) without waiving its right to arbitrate."

If Redwood agrees to NY seat/AAA for arbitration and this provisional carveout language, we can move to signature by next week.

Tom Ellis
VP, Procurement — NimblePay
Attachments: NimblePay_ProvisionalRelief_CommentTable.xlsx (Excel, 24KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: NimblePay MSA — arbitration seat / provisional relief analysis

Team, quick note after reading NimblePay’s counter:

- Risk assessment: NY seat + AAA is reasonable commercially (they’re a US company). For Redwood’s risk tolerance the main exposure is execution risk around emergency injunctive relief (timeline/cost). Allowing emergency court relief is standard and protects Redwood against theft of IP or urgent takedown scenarios.
- Draft language proposal: Keep arbitration for substantive disputes; add: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek provisional injunctive or other provisional relief in the courts of the State of New York or the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, and the parties consent to service of process in accordance with the Order Form."
- Service-of-process: Recommend we tie consent to the Order Form and limit scope to commercial contract disputes (exclude collections). Also add a short notice/cure window for injunctive relief requests where practical.
- Operational ask: If we accept NY/AAA, Sales Ops needs a registry of the registered agent details and Sales must confirm Order Form contact for service-of-process. Laura — please prepare two redline options (A: NY/AAA + provisional carveout, B: Delaware law + provisional carveout + consent to service).

Irene, any litigation flags on venue selection? If we pick NY seat but allow emergency relief in SDNY, we should be comfortable with filing/defense patterns there.

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Contracts Counsel — Redwood Inference

Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cNimblePay-MSA (working redline)

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Maya R. Cortez <maya.cortez@nimblepay.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nimblepay.com>, contracts@nimblepay.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 23 Jun 2028 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Final proposed text — provisional relief carveout + service (NimblePay)

Maya / Tom — following our internal review, please find Redwood’s clean proposal below; we think it preserves both parties’ priorities and is narrow enough to be operational. If you can confirm, we’ll produce a redline to incorporate into the MSA and update the Order Form contact.

Proposed clause (clean):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, either party may seek provisional injunctive or other provisional relief in any court of competent jurisdiction (including courts in New York). The initiation of such proceedings shall not constitute a waiver of the parties’ agreement to arbitrate any dispute. The parties agree that service of process for actions arising out of or relating to this Agreement may be effected in accordance with the contact information set forth on the Order Form, and each party shall maintain a valid agent for service of process in the jurisdiction specified on the Order Form."

Practical notes:
- This preserves NimblePay’s ability to go to NY courts for emergency relief while keeping arbitration for the merits.
- We will not expand consent-to-service beyond contract disputes and will add a short carve for collections as discussed.

Next steps:
1) If NimblePay confirms this wording, Laura will circulate a redline integrating it into the MSA and update the Order Form template with the registered agent block.
2) Kar thik will prepare an Ops checklist (registered agent info, e-mail contact for service, internal escalation for emergency filings).
3) We’ll aim for DocuSign circulation by end of next week if we have sign-off.

Please confirm or mark changes directly in the Google redline (link below). If you prefer a different seat for arbitration (e.g., Delaware), call that out and we’ll produce Option B.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Legal — Redwood Inference

Google redline: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cNimblePay-MSA
